package_info.package_manager: N/A (open-source Android malware, not distributed via official package manager)
package_info.package_versions: All known versions as of June 2024
package_info.why_malicious: Rafel RAT is a remote administration tool designed for malicious purposes, enabling attackers to gain full control over Android devices, exfiltrate sensitive data, conduct surveillance, and deploy ransomware. Its use in espionage and cybercrime campaigns against high-profile targets demonstrates its intent and impact.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after installation, upon device boot or app launch)
execution_context.file_location: Main RAT payload (Android APK main activity/service)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The RAT requests and abuses Android permissions to access contacts, SMS, call logs, camera, microphone, and file storage, then exfiltrates this data to a remote C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code abuses granted Android permissions to collect sensitive user data (contacts, SMS, call logs, files, camera/microphone recordings), then transmits this data to a remote command-and-control server via HTTP/S, enabling espionage and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate apps rarely require or use such a broad set of sensitive permissions, especially for background exfiltration of user data to external servers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Android apps only request permissions necessary for their stated function and do not silently exfiltrate user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise device management tools may request similar permissions, but with user consent and clear notification.
key_indicators: Silent data exfiltration to remote server

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on C2 command or scheduled task)
execution_context.file_location: RAT command handler (background service within APK)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Implements remote command execution, file upload/download, and device control (e.g., lock device, wipe data, install/uninstall apps) via commands received from the C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving commands from the C2 server, the code executes arbitrary actions on the device, such as uploading/downloading files, locking or wiping the device, and installing or uninstalling applications, granting the attacker full remote control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote command execution and device control are hallmarks of RAT malware, not legitimate applications.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not allow remote parties to execute arbitrary commands or control device security features.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Mobile device management (MDM) solutions may have similar capabilities, but are deployed with user and organizational consent.

execution_context.file_location: RAT ransomware module (within APK or loaded dynamically)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Encrypts user files on the device and displays a ransom note, demanding payment for decryption.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a ransomware activation command from the C2 server, the code encrypts user files on the device and displays a ransom note, coercing the victim to pay for file recovery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: File encryption and ransom demands are clear indicators of ransomware activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps never encrypt user files for ransom.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for this behavior in consumer apps.
key_indicators: Demand for payment to restore access

attack_chain.action: Victim installs the malicious APK (Rafel RAT) on their Android device, often via social engineering or trojanized app distribution.
RAT requests and abuses sensitive Android permissions to access user data and device features.
RAT exfiltrates collected data (contacts, SMS, files, etc.) to the attacker's C2 server.
RAT receives and executes remote commands from the C2 server, enabling full device control (file operations, device lock/wipe, app management).
RAT activates ransomware module to encrypt user files and display ransom note, if instructed by attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Android app requesting excessive permissions (contacts, SMS, call logs, device admin, etc.)
Background network connections to known C2 infrastructure
Silent exfiltration of user data (contacts, SMS, files) without user interaction
Remote command execution and device control actions
File encryption and ransom note display
file_indicators: APK files with obfuscated code and suspicious permission requests
Presence of device admin receiver components in manifest
Unusual background services running after app installation
network_indicators: Outbound connections to hardcoded or dynamically resolved C2 domains/IPs
Unusual HTTP/S POST requests containing device data
Beaconing behavior to remote servers after installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications that request a broad set of sensitive permissions, especially device admin rights, and establish persistent background network connections. Analyze app behavior for silent data exfiltration, remote command execution, and file encryption. Use network monitoring to detect connections to known C2 infrastructure and inspect for ransom note artifacts or abnormal file access patterns. Employ mobile security solutions capable of behavioral analysis and static code inspection for RAT and ransomware indicators.
